1. R0.8.5 — adjudication

F32 — ACCEPT the exact closure, but do not confuse it with full lineage provenance

F32 was a real defect:

unique lock holder
!=
unique durable lineage

R0.8.4's lock prevented concurrent current controllers but did not remember which durable history had already become current.

R0.8.5 correctly reproduced the sequential stale-root resurrection:

H0
├─ B -> revision 4 / HB
└─ stale A later reopens H0 and -> revision 4 / HA

and moved the durable lineage fact into the deployment anchor:

anchor:
    revision
    head

A root behind the anchor is refused; equal revision/different head is refused.

Ruling

F32 exact rollback-resurrection defect: CLOSED under the stated single-host deployment-anchor profile.

However, the R0.8.5 repair allows:

root.revision == anchor.revision + 1

as the crash window between root install and anchor update.

The reported R0.8.6 F35 shows why this matters:

one revision ahead proves ordering, not provenance.

A foreign but valid successor can occupy that tolerated one-ahead shape.

Therefore:

F32:
    CLOSED for stale / rollback resurrection

broader successor provenance:
    STILL OPEN as F35

Do not let "F32 closed" promote the broader S3 claim past the evidence.

3. F33 — ACCEPT closure

The R0.8.4 repair committed the observed SQLite schema.

F33 correctly identified the remaining hole:

observed interpreter
!=
intended interpreter

At genesis, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS is initialization, not validation.

R0.8.5 now derives expected_schema() by:

  1. executing the compiled SCHEMA into a pristine in-memory SQLite database;

  2. reading back SQLite's own normalized schema representation;

  3. requiring exact equality against the live store;

  4. doing so before any semantic read or genesis adoption.

This avoids a hand-transcribed schema contract drifting from the compiled schema.

Ruling

F33: CLOSED under the declared trusted/fixed SQLite-engine profile.

This strengthens E-14 beyond R0.8.4.

The remaining trust profile is legitimate:

trusted:
    SQLite engine / built-in interpretation implementation

committed / verified:
    intended schema contract
    canonical semantic rows
    canonical ordering contract

Do not claim resistance to adversarial replacement of the SQLite engine binary itself.

4. F34 — ACCEPT closure under profile

PRAGMA integrity_check must return exactly:

ok

before the store is admitted.

This addresses a different layer than a digest over values: the digest asks SQLite to interpret the structures, while integrity_check checks those structures for internal consistency.

Ruling

F34: CLOSED for the declared correctness profile.

Availability / DoS from a hostile store remains outside this claim.

5. F24 — ACCEPT the proper closure

R0.8.5 no longer delegates canonical ordering to SQLite ORDER BY semantics.

It:

  • reads logical rows;

  • sorts lifecycle / authority by numeric seq;

  • sorts workers by name bytes;

  • sorts ledger by (family, request_id) bytes;

  • refuses duplicate logical keys.

This is materially cleaner than relying on a collation or index traversal.

Ruling

F24: CLOSED for the represented canonical collections.

Keep the negative-control lesson:

a control that changes a connection-local pragma in some other process is not evidence about the controller's own connection.

9. L1 two-witness structure — ACCEPT, with one terminology correction

The v2 adjudication asked for exactly this split:

L1-PRE:
    resolvability / a path exists

L1 temporal:
    eventuality only under a declared fairness policy

v3 now implements that split.

This is the right structure.

What the temporal witness establishes

For the finite model:

NO fairness:
    a stuttering / postponement counterexample exists

WF(finality):
    L1-closed holds
    -> evidenced generation eventually closes or terminalizes

WF(finality) only:
    L1-strict can fail
    -> a closed generation can remain vacant forever

WF(finality) + WF(attach):
    L1-strict holds

NO-FINALITY:
    fairness does not invent a missing finality mechanism

REACH-AS-LOSS:
    progress is possible but violates the safety premise by closing while
    holder is alive

This is a useful separation of safety from liveness.

Terminology defect to fix

The temporal witness repeatedly calls a state:

UNRESOLVABLE

when there is a fair/non-fair infinite counterexample.

That word conflicts with L1-PRE, which already proves the same state has a resolution path.

Without fairness the state is not "unresolvable".

Correct wording:

resolvable:
    YES, a resolution path exists

eventual resolution guaranteed:
    NO, because a non-resolving infinite execution remains admissible

Rename the temporal table column / prose from:

unresolvable

to something like:

bad-fair-path states
nonresolving-counterexample states
eventuality-failing states

and change:

every evidenced state is UNRESOLVABLE

to:

every evidenced state admits a non-resolving stuttering execution when no
fairness assumption excludes postponement

This is a semantic correction, not cosmetic wording.

10. "Clause A is an environment-liveness assumption" — ACCEPT WITH NUANCE

The core finding is right:

the Locus mechanism cannot manufacture a willing successor.

So the existence / availability of a future successor is environmental.

But WF(attach) in the finite model mixes two things:

ENVIRONMENT:
    a valid successor is offered / remains available

SYSTEM / SCHEDULER:
    a continuously enabled valid attach is eventually serviced

Do not classify all of WF(attach) as external.

Recommended split:

ENV-SUCCESSOR:
    eventually a valid willing successor exists / is offered

SYS-ATTACH-FAIRNESS:
    if a valid attach remains continuously enabled, the system does not
    postpone processing it forever

Then:

L1-closed:
    system guarantee under WF(finality)

L1-service-succession:
    system guarantee conditional on ENV-SUCCESSOR + SYS-ATTACH-FAIRNESS

This is a cleaner contract for a real operating environment.

13. E-50 — the two red findings are correct, but split them

E-50 currently combines two distinct gaps.

They should be separated.

E-50a — unresolved same-intent replay policy

Current behavior:

ef_0001:
    UNKNOWN
    effect_key = K

fresh approval:
    ef_0002
    effect_key = K

journal:
    allows ef_0002 to CLAIM / ATTEMPT
    without consulting unresolved ef_0001 by key

Safety therefore depends entirely on the far side.

This violates the stronger S5 discipline unless duplicate risk is explicitly acknowledged.

Important modeling correction

DUPLICATED_ACKNOWLEDGED should probably not be modeled as a terminal state merely because earlier prose called it one.

Risk acknowledgment occurs before the replay's outcome is known.

Prefer an explicit authorization/evidence fact such as:

DUPLICATE_RISK_ACKNOWLEDGED
or
REPLAY_RISK_AUTHORIZED

which permits the new attempt.

That attempt can still later become:

COMMITTED
FAILED
UNKNOWN

If an actual duplicate is later proven, that can have its own outcome/receipt.

E-50b — intent identity vs attempt identity

The first reconciliation run correctly exposed:

same idempotency key
!=
same attempt

A far-side record saying:

ef_0002-a1 completed intent K

must not make the journal claim:

ef_0001-a1 itself COMMITTED

The original attempt needs a distinct terminal relation such as:

SUPERSEDED

while the higher-level intent may be:

SATISFIED / COMMITTED by another attempt

Ruling

Keep both findings red for the Super/ampd lane, but split them in the cross-registry map:

E-50a replay-risk authorization by stable intent identity
E-50b attempt supersession / reconciliation attribution

That will keep two different semantics from sharing one repair.

15. E-43 — measured alternatives expose a better refinement

The adapter results are useful:

A

Scope registration is a world transition.

Pros:

world version again identifies the observable

Cost:

even re-registering the same source currently advances version

B

Scope registry is a separate observable coordinate.

Pros:

resource version semantics stay narrow

Cost:

coarse invalidation;
even unrelated warrants can be refused

Recommendation to TRVM lane

Consider A-idempotent:

if existing scope source digest == new source digest:
    true no-op
    version does not advance

if digest changes:
    scope redefinition is a semantic world transition
    version advances
    log records it

That preserves A's adequacy without charging a semantic transition for an identical registration.

Do not make that change from this lane; hand it to TRVM governance.

16. E-42 — the experiment suggests two orthogonal coordinates, not merely two competing repairs

The adapter results show:

L-PREFIX:
    answers "is this state a descendant of the state the warrant came from?"
    but cannot distinguish an independent byte-identical twin

L-ID:
    answers "is this the same world lineage/birth identity?"
    but refuses a pre-fork warrant even on a legitimate descendant

Those are different questions.

The shipped BOTH adapter already demonstrates:

world/birth identity
+
history/state-prefix identity

can distinguish:

  • an independent twin;

  • a divergent fork;

  • the own lineage.

Recommendation to TRVM lane

Do not force an artificial either/or between L-PREFIX and L-ID.

Adjudicate whether a warrant needs both coordinates:

world_id / lineage_id
+
state-prefix or history digest at issuance

Then define deliberately whether a fork():

A. creates a new world identity
or
B. creates a descendant identity with explicit ancestry

That semantic choice should determine warrant portability.
